summary: Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Toyo University around 1895–1898. He later held a post at Toyo University and founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.

Beiyin Deng works in Buddhist and religious studies, holding degrees from Fudan University (BA), New York University (MA), and Arizona State University (PhD, 2024). Deng served as a Visiting Instructor at Grinnell College before becoming Assistant Professor at the University of Missouri in 2024.

Bela Bhattacharya (born 1950) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Beligalle Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University. He has held posts as Professor at the University of Ruhuna and Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who completed a PhD at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein by 2001. He served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi, a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earned her PhD from SOAS University of London. She held positions at UC Berkeley and the University of Virginia before becoming Senior Lecturer in East Asian Religions at the University of Bristol.
Benhua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a doctoral degree at Nanjing University (2018–2021). Yang holds a post at Anhui University.

Benigno Ferrario (1887–1956) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale". Around 1927–1956, he served as Professor of Classical Languages and Philosophy at the University of the Republic.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from the University of Calcutta and a D.Litt. from the University of London. He was headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution and later Professor at the University of Calcutta.

Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a sinologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held professorships at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program in 2002.

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. (attested 2006). He also studied with Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. Around 2010–2016, he served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan.
Benjamin C. Ray (born 1940) is a religious studies scholar on the faculty of the University of Virginia, where he was attested as Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in 2000.
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

Benjamin Fürchtegott Balthasar von Bergmann (1772–1856) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena before completing his PhD at the University of Tartu by 1816.
Benjamin Goldstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2026).

Benjamin Guy Babington (1794–1866) was an Indologist and linguist who earned an MD at Cambridge. He served as Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1826–1828), founded the Madras Literary Society, and worked as a physician at Guy's Hospital.
Benjamin H. Rice (1814–1887) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Homerton College from 1834 to 1836. In 1836, he served as a teacher and missionary for the London Missionary Society.
